title: Bram and the Letter
premise: Ines Ravensworth, archivist of St. Aldhelm's Cathedral, has a private habit of solving the deaths the police file away as accidents. When a drowned man is pulled from the canal wearing clothes stolen from her own closet, she realizes the killer is staging her — the witness to something buried in the cathedral's locked crypt decades ago. Following a letter hidden in the crypt's foundation stones, Ines uncovers an inheritance fraud that rewrote three families' identities, and discovers the 'dead' witness is alive, hiding as the cathedral's own bell-ringer. The killer is Dean Harrow, protecting the forged will that made him heir; in the crypt's final confrontation, Ines chooses love over duty by sparing the evidence that would also destroy the innocent woman she loves, exposing Harrow through his own staged costume instead.
about_author: Juniper Voss is the pen name of a former parish records clerk who spent eleven years cataloguing births, deaths, and the lies between them. They write mysteries about people who find truth in paperwork no one else bothers to read.

chapters.title: The Fourth Accident
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. She catalogs the drowned man's effects and recognizes her own gray coat on the corpse. Flashbacks establish her three prior unofficial investigations. Emotional beat: cold dread beneath professional calm.

chapters.title: Clothes That Aren't Mine
chapters.summary: Detective Sergeant Okonkwo interviews Ines; she hides how well the stolen garments fit. POV shifts briefly to the morgue attendant noticing the coat was altered to fit someone taller. Beat: paranoia takes root.

chapters.title: The Locked Crypt
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. She petitions the chapter to open the sealed crypt; Dean Harrow refuses with polished charm. She finds fresh scratches on the crypt door's ancient lock. Beat: the institution itself feels complicit.

chapters.title: What the Bells Remember
chapters.summary: Bell-ringer Silas Marsh's POV. He watches Ines from the tower, recognizing her as the child he once saw flee the crypt in 1989. Beat: guilt and protectiveness war in him.

chapters.title: A Letter in the Stones
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Repair work on the north wall exposes a lead tube: a letter naming three heirs dispossessed by a rewritten will. One signature matches the drowned man. Beat: exhilaration curdling into fear.

chapters.title: The Woman in the Archive
chapters.summary: Introduces Maren, the conservator restoring flood-damaged registers, and Ines's growing tenderness toward her. Maren notices a page razored from the 1989 burial register. Beat: warmth as counterweight to dread.

chapters.title: Dead Men Wear Wool
chapters.summary: Okonkwo's POV. Forensics show the drowned man died elsewhere; the canal was a stage set. Someone with archive access knew Ines's measurements. Beat: suspicion falls uncomfortably close to home.

chapters.title: Three Funerals, One Grave
chapters.summary: Ines connects her three earlier 'accidents' to the letter's named heirs — all dead within two years. Beat: the horror of realizing she's been circling this for years without seeing it.

chapters.title: Silas Speaks
chapters.summary: Silas finally approaches Ines at night, half-confessing he witnessed a body carried into the crypt thirty-five years ago but was paid to forget. Beat: trembling relief at shared burden.

chapters.title: Harrow's Hospitality
chapters.summary: Dean Harrow invites Ines to dinner, probing what she knows while revealing fragments of his own fabricated gentry lineage. Beat: velvet menace; Ines performs ignorance.

chapters.title: Maren's Secret
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. She admits she was hired anonymously to destroy the register page — and couldn't. Her confession nearly breaks their trust. Beat: love tested against deception.

chapters.title: The Witness Who Is Dead
chapters.summary: Ines traces the official record: the 1989 witness, Edith Vane, died and was buried — yet the coffin was sealed before viewing. Beat: the certainty that the dead witness lives.

chapters.title: Grave Without a Body
chapters.summary: Okonkwo, now quietly allied with Ines, exhumation paperwork reveals Edith's coffin holds sandbags. Someone powerful signed the order. Beat: institutional rot confirmed.

chapters.title: Tower at Midnight
chapters.summary: Ines climbs to the belfry and finds Edith Vane living there for decades under Silas's protection, aged and sharp, holding the original will. Beat: the myth made flesh.

chapters.title: What Edith Saw
chapters.summary: Edith's testimony: she saw Harrow's father murder the true heir and forge the will; Harrow has killed ever since to keep it. Beat: grief for thirty-five stolen years.

chapters.title: The Trap Sprung
chapters.summary: Someone searches Ines's flat; her copy of the letter is gone. A second body appears, again dressed in her clothes. Beat: the killer is accelerating; she is the intended final victim.

chapters.title: Fracture
chapters.summary: Harrow confronts Maren, offering her immunity to betray Ines. Maren warns Ines instead, and they flee together through the cloisters. Beat: love chosen openly at last.

chapters.title: Down Into the Crypt
chapters.summary: Following Silas's memory of a secondary entrance, Ines and Okonkwo enter the sealed crypt and find the true heir's remains — and Harrow waiting. Beat: claustrophobic dread.

chapters.title: The Weight of Names
chapters.summary: Climax part one. Harrow traps them below, monologuing his inheritance-as-destiny creed. Ines stalls him by attacking his identity: he is no one's heir but a forger's son. Beat: words as weapons.

chapters.title: Bells Over Stone
chapters.summary: Climax part two. Silas rings the alarm peal; Okonkwo and police descend. Harrow tries to drown Ines as he did the others; Edith's testimony and the recovered will break him. Beat: terror turning to deliverance.

chapters.title: Love Against Duty
chapters.summary: Resolution. Ines must decide whether to publish everything, which would expose Maren's hired role. She testifies to Harrow's crimes while shielding Maren, choosing love over archival purity. Beat: costly mercy.

chapters.title: The Open Door
chapters.summary: Epilogue, spring. The crypt opens as a memorial; Edith walks into daylight; Ines and Maren begin cataloguing the truth together. Final image: Ines files the case closed in her private ledger. Beat: quiet, earned peace.
